journal_articles.title: ApoE-dependent lipid handling by median eminence microglia supports myelin remodeling and metabolic function.
journal_articles.abstract: Microglia regulate hypothalamic control of systemic metabolism, but the mechanisms underlying their contribution remain unclear. Here, we identify apolipoprotein E (ApoE)-associated microglial transcriptional states enriched in the median eminence (ME), a brain region involved in sensing peripheral cues and metabolic regulation. These transcriptional states are characterized by programs related to lipid handling, interferon-associated responses, and cellular stress. Consumption of a Western diet (WD) increased microglial lipid accumulation and altered myelin remodeling within the ME, while expression of the human APOE4 isoform exacerbated these changes. Deletion of Apoe altered microglial responses to nutritional stress, supporting a role for ApoE in microglial lipid handling. Finally, activation of liver X receptor using synthetic high-density lipoprotein (sHDL) nanoparticles enhanced microglial lipid-handling programs, improved hypothalamic leptin responsiveness, reduced food intake, and limited weight gain in WD-fed mice. Together, these findings identify ApoE-dependent lipid handling as a key component of adaptive microglial responses to metabolic stress.

journal_articles.title: Arbitrium crosstalk enables shared signaling among phages.
journal_articles.abstract: The arbitrium system has transformed our understanding of phage biology by demonstrating that temperate phages communicate through extracellular peptides to coordinate lysis-lysogeny decisions. Initially considered a highly specific signaling pathway restricted to individual phage lineages, arbitrium communication has now been shown to extend beyond lineage boundaries in some phage systems. Recent studies have shown that non-cognate arbitrium peptides can interact with heterologous receptors, providing evidence of inter-phage crosstalk. Here, we synthesize current knowledge of the molecular basis of arbitrium signaling, the structural determinants of peptide-receptor specificity, and the potential ecological and evolutionary consequences of inter-phage communication. We suggest that arbitrium crosstalk may shape phage ecology by mediating competitive and potentially cooperative interactions within shared signaling environments. We also discuss its potential uses in engineered phage systems, synthetic biology, and microbiome engineering. Collectively, the available evidence broadens the concept of viral communication beyond lineage-specific signaling, while the ecological significance and practical applications of arbitrium crosstalk remain to be established.

journal_articles.title: Cell death in context: From mechanisms to interventions.
journal_articles.abstract: When, how, and why cells die, and what happens when they survive, have profound consequences for development, immunity, and disease. To coincide with the Cell Press Symposium "Taking programmed cell death from mechanisms to interventions," we bring together perspectives from researchers across career stages and areas of cell death research. From emerging mechanisms and consequences of cell death to opportunities for therapeutic intervention, these voices highlight a rapidly evolving field and the questions that will shape its future.

journal_articles.title: Circulating FABP4 promotes obesity-associated breast cancer lung metastasis through PIP2.
journal_articles.abstract: Obesity is a well-established risk factor for increased incidence and mortality in multiple cancers, including breast cancer. However, the key molecular mechanisms linking obesity to breast cancer progression remain incompletely understood. In this study, using several high-fat diet-induced obesity models, we demonstrate that obesity promotes breast cancer lung metastasis through elevated levels of adipocyte-derived circulating FABP4. Mechanistically, circulating FABP4 directly binds to a subset of breast cancer cells via the membrane lipid PIP2. This FABP4/PIP2 interaction activates PKC signaling and enhances mitochondrial ROS production, driving cancer cell migration. Genetic deletion of FABP4, either globally or specifically in adipocytes, markedly reduces obesity-associated metastasis. Moreover, therapeutic targeting of circulating FABP4 using a distinctive neutralizing monoclonal antibody significantly suppresses breast cancer metastasis in multiple preclinical models. Together, these findings identify the FABP4/PIP2 axis as a key mechanism underlying obesity-driven breast cancer and highlight it as a promising therapeutic target for treating metastatic breast cancer.

journal_articles.title: Conserved disordered regions and ubiquitin-binding motifs within HUWE1 contribute to substrate targeting plasticity.
journal_articles.abstract: E3 ligases confer substrate specificity within ubiquitin-dependent pathways. However, the pleiotropic HECT-type E3 ligase HUWE1 targets a biochemically and structurally diverse set of substrates through mechanisms that remain largely unknown. We develop a combinatorial cell-based system integrating global proteomics, proximity labeling, and reporter assays to systematically interrogate HUWE1 sequence features that enable substrate targeting. We define a robust HUWE1 activity signature consisting of putative substrates that accumulate upon HUWE1 impairment across multiple cell lines. By re-expressing a panel of HUWE1 deletion mutants, we find that both the largest intrinsically disordered region and the conserved ubiquitin-binding motifs contribute to substrate targeting. Structural modeling and domain analysis further suggest that HUWE1 achieves targeting plasticity through multivalent interactions, engaging both disordered and structured regions within its substrates. Together, our findings establish a framework for understanding how large, modular E3 ligases exploit intrinsic disorder and multivalency to shape their substrate repertoires.

journal_articles.title: Cysteine promotes islet α-cell glucagon secretion by limiting oxidative inhibition of voltage-gated sodium channels.
journal_articles.abstract: Cysteine serves as a robust α-cell secretagogue. While diabetes alters both plasma cysteine and glucagon levels, the mechanisms of α-cell cysteine action remain unclear. Here, we identified cysteine as a key regulator of islet glucagon secretion through redox control of α-cell electrical excitability. Short-term cysteine depletion markedly suppressed hypoglycemia-stimulated glucagon secretion from both human and mouse islets. Moreover, cysteine-depleted islets showed reduced hypoglycemia-stimulated α-cell calcium (Ca2+) influx. Islet glucagon secretion and α-cell Ca2+ influx rapidly normalized following cysteine restoration. Cysteine depletion also reduced α-cell voltage-gated sodium channel (NaV) conductance and action potential amplitude. Importantly, reducing agents restored NaV currents and glucose control of α-cell Ca2+ handling in islets without cysteine. Together, these findings identify reductive amplification of NaV channels as a key mechanism required for hypoglycemia-stimulated glucagon secretion, highlighting cysteine as a critical regulator of α-cell redox state, electrical excitability, and glucagon secretion.

journal_articles.title: Exposure to immune stimuli augments alveolar macrophages to acquire neutrophil antimicrobial molecules to prevent bacterial pneumonia.
journal_articles.abstract: The protective adaptation of innate immune defenses against respiratory pathogens has been linked to previous exposure to immune stimuli; however, the underlying mechanisms of these adaptations are not yet fully understood. Here, we show that pre-exposure to a low dose of non-specific immune stimuli or infection protects against subsequent lethal methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) challenge. This enhanced protection concurs with increased alveolar macrophages (AMs) resulting from a self-renewal process in the lungs. Importantly, these AMs are programmed to acquire neutrophil-released antimicrobial enzymes from the extracellular space to clear MRSA, prevent tissue damage, and rapidly restore lung homeostasis. AM function depends on differential gene expression, including expression of the efferocytosis receptor Mer proto-oncogene tyrosine kinase (MerTK) and the anti-apoptotic regulator Bcl-xL. Thus, our data highlight that AMs acquire neutrophil enzymes as an integral component of innate immune adaptation.

journal_articles.title: HRS dephosphorylation at membrane contact sites promotes sorting within multivesicular endosomes.
journal_articles.abstract: HRS is a receptor tyrosine kinase substrate and ESCRT machinery component. It enables sorting of ubiquitylated cargo into multivesicular endosomes (MVEs) for lysosomal degradation but also functions in receptor recycling. We show that co-depletion of its ESCRT-0 binding partners, STAM1 and STAM2, recapitulates defects in EGF receptor (EGFR) sorting onto intraluminal vesicles (ILVs) but does not mirror the increased MVE size evident after HRS depletion. Using mutagenesis of the endogenous gene or introduction of APEX2-tagged HRS variants, we find that HRS Y329/334 phosphorylation is dispensable for EGFR sorting and MVE size control. AnnexinA1 mediates ER:endosomal membrane contacts and promotes EGF-stimulated ILV formation. We show that reduced ILV formation on AnnexinA1 depletion is accompanied by increased HRS phosphorylation, likely through reduced HRS dephosphorylation by ER-localised PTP1B. Conversely, Y329/334 mutation renders ILV formation insensitive to AnnexinA1 depletion. Our data suggest that rapid HRS dephosphorylation at ER:MVE contacts promotes efficient ILV formation.

journal_articles.title: IDO1 methylation by EZH2 confers resistance to its targeted therapy in colorectal cancer through tryptophan-kynurenine metabolic rewiring.
journal_articles.abstract: Deciphering cancer metabolic reprogramming mechanisms can identify new targets to potentiate EZH2 inhibitor efficacy. Using an in vivo genome-wide CRISPR loss-of-function screen in a CRC mouse model, we pinpointed IDO1 as a key mediator of EZH2 inhibitor resistance. EZH2 blockade remodeled CRC cell metabolism by upregulating IDO1 protein and hyperactivating the tryptophan-kynurenine pathway. Both genetic and pharmacological inhibition of IDO1 suppressed tumor growth and rescued EZH2 inhibitor resistance in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, EZH2 directly binds and methylates IDO1. Methylation of IDO1 facilitates IDO1 ubiquitination and subsequent degradation. Accordingly, EZH2 inhibition stabilizes IDO1, augments tryptophan-kynurenine metabolic flux, and ultimately confers therapeutic resistance. In summary, our study identifies IDO1 as a non-histone substrate of EZH2 methyltransferase activity and validates that disrupting IDO1-mediated tryptophan metabolism is a viable strategy to overcome EZH2 targeted therapy resistance in cancers.

journal_articles.title: Influenza virus antagonizes self-sensing by RIG-I to enhance viral replication.
journal_articles.abstract: Innate immune sensors must finely distinguish pathogens from the host to mount a response only during infection. RIG-I is a cytoplasmic sensor that triggers a broad antiviral response in response to sensing foreign RNAs. Here, we show that RIG-I not only binds viral RNAs but is activated by host RNAs. These are primarily non-coding RNAs transcribed by RNA polymerase III. They are benign under normal conditions but become immunogenic during influenza virus infection, where they signal via RIG-I to suppress viral replication. These RNAs are also bound by influenza virus nucleoprotein (NP), which normally functions to encapsidate the viral genome. NP interacts with RIG-I via an RNA bridge and antagonizes sensing of self-RNAs to counter innate immune responses. Overall, we demonstrate that self-sensing is strategically deployed by the cell to amplify the antiviral response and reveal a newly identified viral countermeasure that disrupts RIG-I activation by host RNAs.

journal_articles.title: MHC II-expressing bone marrow megakaryocytes are noncanonical antigen-presenting cells and activate CD4+ T cells ex vivo.
journal_articles.abstract: While professional antigen-presenting cells drive adaptive immunity, atypical cell types can fulfill this role in the bone marrow. Megakaryocytes (MKs) are canonically recognized for platelet production, but recent studies indicate functional heterogeneity and immune potential. We found that ∼20% of bone marrow MKs express major histocompatibility complex (MHC) II and co-stimulatory receptors CD80, CD86, CD40, and CD83. These MKs process and present antigen to activate T cells ex vivo in an MHC II-dependent manner. MK/T cell interactions induced TGF-β1 secretion and promoted induced regulatory T cell (Treg) differentiation. Toll-like receptor (TLR) stimulation of MKs elicited modest Th1-associated responses, including IFN-γ and TNF-α production, without robust Th17 differentiation. Immunopeptidomics confirmed peptide occupancy of MK MHC II in vivo. Using MK-targeted MHC II deletion, we observed altered TLR responses and reduced bone marrow TGF-β1. Together, these findings identify MHC II+ MKs as noncanonical antigen-presenting cells with potential roles in regulating CD4+ T cell responses within the bone marrow niche.

journal_articles.title: Macrophages iron out cancer cells' vulnerability.
journal_articles.abstract: Surviving despite accumulating toxic metabolites inside the cell is a defining feature of cancer evolution. In the current issue of Cell Reports, Eric Cheung and coworkers identify a mechanism that enables the survival of malignant pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) cells through the sequestration of reactive iron.1.

journal_articles.title: Pot1a maintains mesenchymal stem cell niche function to support hematopoietic stem cells.
journal_articles.abstract: Hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) maintain their function through interactions with niche cells in the bone marrow. We previously demonstrated that protection of telomeres 1a (Pot1a), a shelterin component, maintains HSCs and neuron-glial antigen 2-expressing (NG2+) mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) by suppressing DNA damage response (DDR) and reactive oxygen species (ROS) production. However, the role of Pot1a in leptin receptor-expressing (LepR+) MSCs, a primary HSC niche component, remains unclear. LepR-specific Pot1a knockout mice showed decreased LepR+ MSC numbers, increased DDR and ROS production, reduced HSC quiescence, and impaired long-term hematopoietic reconstitution. In contrast, cell-permeable Pot1a enhanced the hematopoietic-supporting function of LepR+ MSCs. Pot1a deficiency reduced pleiotrophin (Ptn) expression, whereas Pot1a overexpression increased its expression. These findings suggest that Pot1a preserves LepR+ MSC function by limiting stress-associated changes, maintaining MSC numbers, and regulating hematopoietic-supportive factor expression, including PTN.

journal_articles.title: Programmed bacterial lysis in vivo alters host immune responses and microbial pathogenesis.
journal_articles.abstract: Vibrio cholerae injects toxic type VI secretion system (T6SS) effectors to lyse sensitive intestinal commensals, but how this bacterial antagonism enhances mucosal host immune responses and its pathogenicity remains unknown. To mimic T6SS-mediated killing, we engineered V. cholerae lysis strains by using CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) to knockdown essential genes in peptidoglycan biogenesis or lipopolysaccharide (LPS) transport. Our results indicate that controlled bacterial lysis in vivo leads to divergent mucosal immune responses that directly modulate colonization and pathogenicity of a bystander, non-lysing V. cholerae ΔT6SS strain. Mass spectrometric analysis of the lysis debris revealed proinflammatory muropeptides correlating with these changes. We confirmed that oral co-administration of a synthetic peptidoglycan-derived metabolite with a V. cholerae ΔT6SS mutant, but not the wild type, shows dramatic enhancement of disease symptoms. These findings show that intestinal exposure to discrete bacterial cell wall metabolites can differentially modulate host innate immune responses and consequently bacterial pathogenesis.

journal_articles.title: Rheb in central amygdala somatostatin neurons regulates chronic itch and anxiety-like behaviors.
journal_articles.abstract: Chronic itch represents a significant clinical challenge that substantially impairs patients' quality of life, yet its underlying neural circuit and molecular mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we demonstrate that somatostatin-expressing (SST) neurons in the central amygdala (CeA) are activated and functionally required in a mouse model of diphenylcyclopropenone (DCP)-induced chronic itch. Transcriptomic profiling further revealed upregulation of Ras homolog enriched in brain (Rheb) within DCP-TRAPed CeA SST neurons. Notably, Rheb knockdown suppressed the hyperexcitability of CeA SST neurons and alleviated chronic itch-related scratching and anxiety-like behaviors in DCP-treated mice. Conversely, Rheb overexpression promoted scratching and anxiety-like behaviors in naive mice. Collectively, these findings delineate a Rheb-regulated CeA SST neuronal mechanism that contributes to chronic itch-related scratching and anxiety-like behaviors, highlighting a potential molecular target for therapeutic intervention in chronic itch.

journal_articles.title: Tau-driven hyperexcitability of locus coeruleus noradrenergic neurons underlies sleep fragmentation and cognitive decline in mice.
journal_articles.abstract: Early sleep disruption is a hallmark of preclinical Alzheimer's disease (AD), but its underlying mechanisms are unclear. The locus coeruleus (LC) dopamine-β-hydroxylase noradrenergic (LCDBH) neurons are vulnerable to early tau pathology in AD. Using P301S transgenic mice and cell-type-specific tau overexpression models, we show that pathological tau accumulation selectively increases the intrinsic excitability of LCDBH neurons. Tau-induced neuronal hyperactivity disrupts sleep homeostasis, reduces non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep and slow-wave activity, increases sleep fragmentation and microarousals, and delays both anesthetic induction and sleep onset. Furthermore, tau overexpression in LCDBH neurons leads to significant recognition memory deficits. Notably, optogenetic suppression of LCDBH-tau neuronal activity reverses sleep disturbances and rescues cognitive dysfunction. Our findings demonstrate that tau-driven hyperexcitability of LCDBH neurons is a core driver of early sleep and cognitive impairments in AD, providing a mechanistic insight and potential target for preclinical AD treatment.

journal_articles.title: Temporal shifts in post-asthmatic immune responses define tumor outcomes via strain-specific monocyte reprogramming.
journal_articles.abstract: Epidemiological evidence linking asthma to lung cancer risk remains contradictory, presenting asthma as either a risk factor or a protective condition. We hypothesize that this heterogeneity stems from the temporal dynamics of inflammatory response and host genetic background. Using ovalbumin (OVA)-induced asthma models, we identify a temporal shift in immune effectors driving post-asthmatic tumorigenesis. During acute airway inflammation, eosinophil infiltration accelerates tumor growth across mouse strains. Following resolution, however, tumorigenic outcomes in recovery diverge along genetic lines. Prior asthma reshapes chromatin landscapes of bone marrow myeloid progenitors, establishing innate immune memory that differentially programs monocytes across strains. In C57BL/6 mice, trained monocytes adopt oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), acquiring a suppressive, tissue-remodeling phenotype that promotes tumor progression. Conversely, BALB/c-trained monocytes utilize glycolysis to maintain a pro-phagocytic state, enabling tumor clearance. These findings delineate a biphasic mechanism wherein temporal shifts in post-asthmatic immune responses define tumor outcomes via strain-specific monocyte metabolic reprogramming.

journal_articles.title: Terms and conditions apply: A cytokine cocktail licenses astrocyte antigen presentation.
journal_articles.abstract: Whether astrocytes are fully competent antigen-presenting cells has been debated for over four decades. Fisher et al. show they are, but only conditionally: IFN-γ and microglial cytokines are jointly required, and stimulated astrocytes drive antigen-specific expansion of CD4+ T cells.

journal_articles.title: The DUF2439/RADIF domain of ZGRF1 is a RAD51 interactor and facilitator.
journal_articles.abstract: DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) are extremely toxic DNA lesions that can cause loss of genetic information and cell death if left unrepaired. During S and G2 phases of the cell cycle, DSBs can be repaired by homologous recombination (HR). The human zinc finger GRF-type containing 1 (ZGRF1) helicase and RAD54B translocase both promote HR. Here, we report that the DUF2439 domain, shared by ZGRF1 and RAD54B, interacts with RAD51 in vitro, and provides resistance to the DNA interstrand-crosslinking agent mitomycin C (MMC). Furthermore, the DUF2439 domain is necessary for recruitment of ZGRF1 to MMC-induced foci. Finally, we show synergistic roles for ZGRF1 and RAD54B in facilitating homology-directed repair of a defined DSB, consistent with the reduced survival of double-mutant cells after treatment with MMC or the PARP inhibitor talazoparib. Based on these results, we propose that the DUF2439 domain recruits ZGRF1 and RAD54B to DNA lesions, where they facilitate RAD51 function to promote HR.

journal_articles.title: The complexity of cerebral small vessel disease: In search of the ideal mouse model.
journal_articles.abstract: Currently, there are few animal models that reflect the physiological complexity of cerebral small vessel disease. Ruan et al.1 presented a pericyte-specific knockout of laminin-γ1 that exhibited several key disease-typical characteristic features at 11 months of age.

journal_articles.title: The enemy of my friend is … my friend? Host phage-microbiome symbiosis: An unexpected story of mutualism and betrayal.
journal_articles.abstract: How does a host turn a beneficial symbiont into a nutrient source? In this issue of Cell Reports, Zhu et al. describe a novel symbiotic mechanism where an animal hijacks a prophage in its symbiont, which triggers lysis and nutrient release.

journal_articles.title: Theta-based organization of information in the frontal cortex.
journal_articles.abstract: Theta (4-10 Hz) oscillations seem to coordinate activity across long-range distances. It is less clear how theta coordinates activity more locally within frontal subareas. We examined activity in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC), ventrolateral prefrontal cortex (vlPFC), and frontal eye fields (FEFs) as non-human primates categorized dot patterns. We characterized how theta coordinates activity within frontal cortex. First, theta phase selectively couples to behaviorally relevant information in spiking. Second, theta influences move in a posterior direction during choices (i.e., dlPFC/vlPFC to FEF) and after correct outcomes (i.e., dlPFC to FEF), but not after errors. Instead, anterior-direction (i.e., FEF to vlPFC) theta influences are stronger after errors. Third, theta participates in behaviorally associated nested cross-frequency interactions. Theta couples to beta (15-30 Hz) oscillations during choices and after errors, whereas beta couples to gamma (40-90 Hz) oscillations after correct outcomes. Our results position theta as a critical mechanism that flexibly and dynamically coordinates activity in frontal cortex.

journal_articles.title: eHLAstic reveals an extended canonical and non-canonical HLA-E immunopeptidome in human cancers.
journal_articles.abstract: HLA-E is a non-classical MHC class I molecule with restricted polymorphism, offering a putative path to broadly applicable off-the-shelf therapies. Yet, the wider HLA-E peptide repertoire remains poorly defined and is largely assumed restricted to signal peptide-derived sequences. We developed eHLAstic, a dedicated HLA-E-binding predictor, that improved the precision of HLA-E ligand discovery almost 3-fold compared with existing approaches. Using eHLAstic and orthogonal biochemical validation, we report 30 previously unrecognized canonical and non-canonical HLA-E-associated peptides, including six cancer-restricted ligands detected in acute lymphoblastic and myeloid leukemia but not healthy blood or bone marrow cells. Most identified ligands were shared across individuals with diverse HLA backgrounds and were detected across hematological and solid cancers. All but one non-canonical ligands were detected exclusively in cancer-associated samples and not in healthy tissues. These findings redefine the HLA-E ligandome and uncover canonical and non-canonical HLA-E ligands with potential for immune recognition and therapeutic targeting.

journal_articles.title: The AMPK-ALDH7A1 axis drives metabolic reprogramming and anti-tumor immunity in hepatocellular carcinoma via KDM5C inhibition.
journal_articles.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction is a feature of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet how respiratory suppression arises remains unclear. Here, we identify an evolutionarily conserved metabolic-epigenetic axis integrating metabolic regulation with tumor suppression and anti-tumor immunity. Through comparative studies in yeast, HCC cell lines, and orthotopic/autochthonous HCC mouse models, we demonstrate that AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK)/Snf1-mediated phosphorylation of aldehyde dehydrogenase ALDH7A1/Ald6 promotes its nuclear translocation and local acetate production, leading to inhibition of histone lysine demethylase KDM5C/Jhd2. This results in H3K4 trimethylation (H3K4me3) accumulation at respiratory genes, activating their transcription and maintaining mitochondrial function. During HCC pathogenesis, loss of AMPK signaling disrupts this pathway, impairing ALDH7A1 nuclear translocation and enabling KDM5C-mediated respiratory suppression. Notably, AMPK-ALDH7A1-acetate-mediated KDM5C inhibition also potentiates cyclic guanosine monophosphate (GMP)-AMP synthase (cGAS)-stimulator of interferon genes (STING) signaling, driving CD8+ T cell infiltration and synergizing with immune checkpoint blockade. Our work defines the evolutionarily conserved AMPK-ALDH7A1-KDM5C axis and establishes acetate as a dual regulator of mitochondrial metabolism and anti-tumor immunity, offering therapeutic strategies for targeting metabolic vulnerabilities in HCC.

journal_articles.title: A conserved flowering-time module underlies double-season cropping.
journal_articles.abstract: Adapting crops to intensive cultivation systems under climate change requires varieties that combine yield potential with optimized flowering and maturation1,2. In central and eastern China, barley has long been cultivated in a double-season cropping system, in which early flowering and maturation are critical for escaping presummer terminal heat stress and enabling flexible rotation with summer crops3,4. Here we trace the genomic footprints of 80 years of modern breeding in China using 505 representative cultivars and identify a flowering-time module defined by a single amino acid substitution in PHYTOCHROME C in combination with a winter-type VERNALIZATION 1 haplotype that underpins this adaptation. The derived allele accelerates heading and maturity, and its frequency has risen sharply in modern autumn-sown varieties. Using base editing in barley and wheat, we confirm causality and demonstrate that this flowering-time combination module, PhyC-VRN1, is functionally conserved across Triticeae. Our results identify and experimentally validate a breeding-relevant flowering-time module that has been selected during modern breeding to enable intensive crop rotations, as well as demonstrate how precision genome editing can be used to reconstruct such adaptive modules for climate-resilient crop design.

journal_articles.title: A two-dimensional reticular triaxial molecularly woven fabric.
journal_articles.abstract: Inspired by macroscopic weaving techniques1-4, molecular weaving, which interlaces molecular strands into ordered networks, has emerged as a powerful strategy for designing functional materials with emergent properties5,6. However, so far, molecular weaving has relied mainly on linear building blocks and biaxial structures. Higher-order weaving (≥3 axes) of nonlinear building blocks is expected to produce intriguing architectures and bring new and unforeseen functions to the resulting materials; however, their construction and property investigation remain underexplored. Here we report a two-dimensional reticular triaxial woven polymer network constructed by incorporating C3-symmetric macrocycles into the woven structure through dative B-N polymerization. The resulting material not only exhibits unique topological chirality and robust mechanical properties but it also serves as a porous material that permits the separation of representative aromatic/aliphatic compounds. This functional utility highlights how higher-order triaxial woven topologies can provide unique advantages in terms of regulating material properties and introduces an extra topological dimension for the construction of functional materials.

journal_articles.title: Accelerating commercialization and deployment of indoor photovoltaics.
journal_articles.abstract: The growing reliance on distributed electronics, such as Internet of Things (IoT) nodes, smart-home devices and portable consumer products, has intensified demand for indoor energy-harvesting technologies that reduce battery replacement and servicing. Consequently, indoor photovoltaics (PVs) have advanced rapidly; however, translating state-of-the-art cells into deployable products requires design principles that reflect real indoor conditions. Here recent progress in perovskite (bulk and quantum dot), organic, amorphous-silicon, III-V and dye-sensitized PVs is examined to identify bottlenecks that arise under low-light conditions and during scale-up. This Review highlights how low-light operation favours wide-bandgap absorbers and reduced non-radiative voltage losses while reshaping module design: lower series-resistance (RS) penalties permit wider subcells and fewer interconnections, increasing geometric fill factor, whereas shunt and leakage pathways consume more of the weak photocurrent. Measurement practices for credible cross-technology benchmarking are discussed, emphasizing the transparent reporting of spectra, illuminance/irradiance, stabilization and uncertainty. Finally, the relationship between device performance and manufacturability and product integration is considered, including power-management requirements and chemical/regulatory constraints (for example, restricted substances and end-of-life handling). These guidelines provide a practical framework for evaluating indoor PVs on the basis of delivered and retained power and for accelerating the transition from laboratory-scale demonstrations to reliable, visually adaptable products for the built environment.

journal_articles.title: Aggression experience and observation drive shared behavioural and neural changes.
journal_articles.abstract: The ability to observe the social behaviour of others and use observed information to bias future action is a fundamental building block of social cognition1-3. Aggression observation activates hypothalamic neurons relevant for aggression control4,5, but whether observation and experience engage common circuit mechanisms that promote a new shared behavioural policy is unclear. Here we develop a strategy to perform large-scale cell-type-specific recordings across subcortical networks for social behaviour generation and learning. We record longitudinally while animals train through direct aggression experience or observation, then probe shared differences in behaviour and neural activity in a novel aggression context. After training, we detect unique signatures of a shared adaptive behavioural strategy that is absent in animals without training. During aggression observation, observed behaviour recruits widespread activation across subcortical networks for behavioural generation and mimics activity evoked by experienced behaviour, and shared neural changes persist into the novel aggression context. Multiregion modelling reveals shared changes to a core aggression network across both experience and observation, including a widespread reduction in inhibition, which we find is necessary for adaptive behavioural change. Together, this demonstrates that experience-like activity during aggression observation can recruit a shared inhibitory plasticity mechanism that biases behaviour toward adaptive proactive behavioural strategies.

journal_articles.title: An AI-native experimental laboratory for autonomous biomolecular operations.
journal_articles.abstract: Developing artificial intelligence (AI)-native experimental laboratories for autonomous scientific exploration with minimal human intervention represents a long-standing goal. Although autonomous experimental systems are emerging1-4, especially in chemical and materials science, they remain largely confined to domains with singular objectives, well-defined workflows and simple instrumentation. This limitation may reflect an 'add-on' architecture that uses AI as a task-specific tool rather than providing it with a global understanding of experiments, especially under engineering-oriented circumstances. Here we present AutoDNA, an AI-native autonomous biomolecular engineering laboratory targeting multi-objective experiments across diverse instruments. Through the co-design of models, experiments and instruments, AutoDNA realizes the co-evolution of AI and the automation system within an end-to-end multi-user framework. The system autonomously orchestrates over 20 types of instruments across more than 11,000 steps to execute core nucleic acid operations including synthesis, transcription, amplification and sequencing, while human intervention is limited to hardware maintenance tasks, such as reagent and labware replenishment. Across four representative applications, AutoDNA matched expert-optimized enzymatic DNA synthesis yields, accelerated concurrent protocol execution by 3.2-fold, completed an end-to-end DNA data storage cycle with exact recovery of the original digital content, and identified and validated a clinically detected KRAS G13D mutation. AutoDNA establishes a blueprint towards science-as-a-service, accelerating biological discovery and advancing various applications in synthetic biology and information storage.

journal_articles.title: Cancer-selective gene circuits via intrinsic ribosomal frameshifting.
journal_articles.abstract: Ribosomal frameshifting, an uncommon translational recoding event, is best known for its regulatory roles in viral gene expression1,2, whereas its physiological relevance in mammals remains poorly understood. Here we show that specific codon pairs trigger efficient -1 frameshifting preferentially in cancer cells. Mechanistically, this recoding arises from ribosomal pausing associated with tRNA and amino acid availability, and is amplified by impaired ribosome quality control and sustained phosphorylation of ribosomal protein S6. We found that this codon-pair-specific frameshifting represents an intrinsic state of translational dysregulation, which is prevalent across cancer cells and reshapes protein synthesis. Taking advantage of this frameshifting-permissive state in cancer cells, we engineered a frameshifting-activated synthetic therapeutic circuit (FAST) that conditionally expresses the pyroptotic effector gasdermin D. FAST is activated across diverse cancer cell types, inducing potent and selective pyroptosis, while sparing normal tissues from detectable toxicity. As a proof of concept, systemic AAV9-mediated delivery of FAST in mouse models of colorectal and pancreatic cancer elicited pronounced tumour regression, robust immune activation and synergistic effects with immune checkpoint blockade. Collectively, these findings reveal codon-pair-dependent ribosomal frameshifting as a feature of translational dysregulation in cancer cells and establish translation-coupled gene circuits as a strategy for cancer-selective therapy.

journal_articles.title: Carbon radical generation by irreversible metal-to-ligand charge transfer.
journal_articles.abstract: Metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT) is a fundamental photoinduced process that underpins a broad range of energy- or electron-transfer events1,2. In the absence of productive substrate engagement, the MLCT excited state typically relaxes to the ground state via photophysical deactivation, reflecting its largely reversible character3,4. Here we report a class of isolable copper-heteroaryl sulfone complexes that, upon visible light irradiation, undergo an irreversible MLCT-driven fragmentation through C-S bond cleavage within the coordinated sulfone ligand, generating carbon-centered radicals. Spectroscopic and computational studies support the formation of MLCT-derived excited states and a low-barrier pathway for C-S bond cleavage. This reactivity is largely independent of the reduction potentials of the corresponding free sulfones, enabling the generation of fluoroalkyl and non-fluorinated tertiary, secondary, and primary (even methyl) alkyl radicals. We demonstrate the utility of this platform in copper-catalyzed C-H fluoroalkylation of arenes and terminal alkynes. Leveraging these MLCT-generated trifluoromethyl radicals to initiate halogen-atom transfer (XAT) from perfluorocyclobutyl iodide (I-FCB), we also achieve radical perfluorocyclobutylation-iodination of alkenes, addressing a longstanding challenge in the incorporation of perfluorocyclobutyl motifs.

journal_articles.title: Comprehensive mapping of essential-gene interactions in M. tuberculosis.
journal_articles.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis, the causative agent of tuberculosis, remains the world's deadliest pathogen1. Despite intensive study, many of its genes remain uncharacterized, which limits the insight that can be gained into tuberculosis biology and constrains drug development. Genetic interaction (GI) mapping is a powerful strategy to define functional relationships between genes by quantifying how the phenotypic effects of combined perturbations deviate from expectations based on single-gene perturbations2,3. Here we develop a dual-sgRNA CRISPR-interference platform that enables high-throughput GI mapping in mycobacteria. We address key technical challenges in library construction and data interpretation by incorporating unique barcodes for each sgRNA pair and implementing a robust statistical pipeline for GI detection. Focusing on essential genes, we generate comprehensive GI maps in the model mycobacterium Mycobacterium smegmatis and the pathogen M. tuberculosis. These maps recapitulate known biology, uncover thousands of previously unrecognized interactions and identify functional connections between essential genes and drug targets. By generating AlphaFold3-based protein-protein interaction predictions4 for all gene pairs in our GI maps, we show that a subset of GIs is likely to reflect underlying physical associations. Validation of selected GIs confirms both novel biological relationships and opportunities for synergistic targeting. Overall, this work establishes a generalizable framework for dual-gene perturbation and defines the architecture of essential-gene networks in mycobacteria, advancing both our understanding of tuberculosis biology and the rational design of combination therapies.

journal_articles.title: Conjugation-regulated self-assembled molecules for tandem solar cells.
journal_articles.abstract: Perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells on rough textured substrates are at present limited by a critical trade-off in self-assembled monolayer (SAM) design because increasing molecular conjugation enhances conductivity but often leads to unfavourable aggregation that impairs conformal coverage1,2. Here we overcome this challenge using a rationally engineered molecular spatial conjugation that incorporates tailored intramolecular distortion to suppress excess π-π stacking without sacrificing charge-transport efficiency. This steric regulation facilitates the formation of a highly ordered, conformal SAM across rough pyramidal textures. By reconciling molecular packing with interfacial coverage, the tailored interface provides optimized energy-level alignment for ultrafast charge extraction, enables improved defect passivation through adaptive conformational adjustment and acts as a robust template for high-quality perovskite film growth. Making use of this interface, the optimized tandem device achieves a notable fill factor (FF) of 85%, yielding a certified stabilized power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 35.1%. Furthermore, the device demonstrates outstanding stability, retaining more than 94% of its initial performance after 1,500 h of ageing under the ISOS-L-1 protocol. Our findings provide a clear molecular engineering route to reconcile conductivity and film uniformity while maximizing the performance of tandem photovoltaics on textured silicon substrates.

journal_articles.title: Diet at disease onset determines tissue inflammatory memory.
journal_articles.abstract: Obesity, which is often associated with prolonged exposure to an obesogenic diet, substantially alters immunity1-7, but whether brief dietary changes shape acute inflammatory responses and long-term tissue memory remains unclear. Here we show that transient high-fat diet (HFD) exposure at the onset of acute type 17 skin inflammation exacerbates disease in lean mice to levels comparable to those associated with chronic obesity. This effect is restricted to a discrete 4-day peri-initiation window; HFD outside this window has no impact, whereas switching obese mice to a low-fat diet (LFD) during a similar window fully blunts disease amplification. Mechanistically, HFD rapidly recruits neutrophils into the skin, and neutrophils in challenged skin express high levels of Nlrp3 (ref. 8) and Il1b. Neutrophil depletion, genetic Nlrp3 deficiency and pharmacological NLRP3 inhibition each blunt the HFD-induced inflammatory amplification. These findings nominate a neutrophil-NLRP3-IL-1β axis that licences pathogenic IL-1R1+CD4+ T helper type 17 (TH17) cells9,10. After recovery, a chromatin-poised tissue-resident memory T cell population persists. Consequently, mice exposed to HFD at disease onset develop exaggerated inflammation upon recurrence, despite recovery and maintenance on LFD. Transient HFD similarly amplifies lung TH17 inflammation through neutrophil- and IL-1R1-dependent mechanisms. Together, these findings show that dietary state during a narrow temporal window can durably reprogram disease trajectory, suggesting that short-lived physiological states may become embedded in local immune memory11 when they coincide with tissue inflammation.

journal_articles.title: Hard X-ray attosecond metrology.
journal_articles.abstract: Sub-ångström spatial resolution combined with attosecond temporal resolution enables direct observation of electron motion in matter1. Attosecond hard X-ray pulses generated at X-ray free-electron laser sources provide the requisite spatiotemporal sensitivity, yet their application has been limited by the absence of precise pulse metrology and control. Here, building on a broadband X-ray split-delay line, we establish metrology of attosecond hard X-ray pulses. Field-correlation measurements provide the first time-domain characterization of the pulse coherence time and demonstrate attosecond synchronization between the generated pulse pairs. By exploiting non-sequential two-photon absorption as a nonlinear probe, intensity autocorrelation quantifies the average pulse duration directly in the time domain to be 170 as. The demonstrated experimental tools and techniques enable systematic attosecond time-resolved experiments, including X-ray pump-X-ray probe spectroscopy and diffraction, and open a pathway to probing electronic phenomena with unprecedented spatial-temporal resolution.

journal_articles.title: Hydrogen Derivatives Enable Cost-Effective Carbon Neutrality in China.
journal_articles.abstract: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change recommended 1.5°C carbon reduction target, requiring powerful enforcement from major economies. China, the largest CO2 emitter, is facing severe difficulties for both variable renewable accommodation and decarbonization of hard-to-abate sectors. Hydrogen, as a critical green energy carrier bridging renewable to end-users, faces significant obstacles in real-world deployment such as costly transportation, storage and fuel-cell adoption. Affordable and coordinated hydrogen deployment plan to accelerate the carbon-neutral transition remains ambiguous. Here, we present cost-effective carbon-neutral transition pathways for entire energy economy of China emphasizing the significant role of hydrogen and derivatives as green energy carriers, considering high-resolution renewable deployments, hourly power system operations in 29 provincial regions, over 46,000 rail/road/marine/pipeline transfer routing of hydrogen derivatives, process-level fuel adoption strategies in all end-use sectors. Results show that incorporating hydrogen and derivatives can reduce the overall transition cost by $ 10.7 trillion compared with renewable and electrification pathways, achieving negative carbon abatement costs ($-6.15/ton), eliminating external oil import expenses, equivalent to over 50% of China trade surplus (2023 level)1, significantly boosting employment and economic growth. Hydrogen derivative based transition pathway offers a vital direction for affordable and secure decarbonization for China and beyond under volatile international energy markets.

journal_articles.title: Imaging exoplanets below the telescope stability limit.
journal_articles.abstract: Exoplanet imaging is the main method for detailed characterization of planets orbiting beyond 1 AU (ref. 1) but it requires suppressing the bright glare of the star to see the faint planet light. As well as sophisticated instrumentation2,3, effective image processing is necessary for starlight suppression, which continues to be a substantial limitation4. Standard algorithms use reference images for starlight modelling and thus they are limited by inevitable telescope instabilities that change from reference to science observation5,6. Addressing this challenge will increase the number of planets amenable to direct imaging and will be a notable step towards imaging exo-Earths with future observatories7. Here we present a new physics-based method for starlight subtraction. Our method combines a multistep optimization with a flexible physical model to produce a starlight model, allowing modelling and compensation of instrument instabilities. We use automatic differentiation (autodiff)8 to optimize millions of model parameters. We demonstrate our method on observations from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) Near-InfraRed Camera (NIRCam)9-11 coronagraph instrument. We achieve sensitivity 2-15 times superior to standard techniques, including the first detection of 51 Eridani b (ref. 12) at 4.3 μm. This is the first time, to our knowledge, that such an approach has demonstrated substantially improved sensitivity on real, on-sky coronagraphic imaging. Our framework can be extended to other current and future ground-based and space-based observatories, including the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope and the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO), potentially relaxing the unprecedented stability requirements needed to make these a success.

journal_articles.title: Multimodal X-ray imaging reveals hierarchical fibre mechanics.
journal_articles.abstract: Fibrous materials, ranging from connective tissues1-4 to engineered composites5-8, are vital to many biological and man-made systems, optimized to withstand complex in operando or in vivo loading. The load-bearing capacity of intervertebral discs (IVDs) of the spine depends on a hierarchical extracellular matrix, where plywood-like lamellae of collagen fibres in the annulus fibrosus contain nanometre-scale fibrils built from staggered triple-helical monomers4,9,10. How intact IVDs couple fibril-scale mechanics to fibre-scale organization under load remains unresolved. Here we introduce TomoSAXS, a full-field 3D small-angle X-ray scattering tomography that maps fibril-to-fibre mechanics across an intact tissue. We show that intrafibrillar molecular pre-strain (D-period stagger) is lamellar textured and tightly correlated with microscale fibre strain. Pre-strain is inversely related to fibril strain and its variability, consistent with load-sharing through molecular unwinding. Radial strain bridges and high-curvature zones at the annulus fibrosus-nucleus pulposus interfaces emerge as critical regulators of local mechanics. These findings reveal concerted fibril-fibre interactions that sustain mechanical equilibrium in the IVD, preserving elasticity and shape. More broadly, TomoSAXS establishes a platform to visualize nanoscale-to-microscale matrix mechanics across biological and synthetic fibrous materials, with applications in ageing and disease, therapeutic evaluation and the design of bio-based and bio-inspired materials.

journal_articles.title: Nectin-4 mediates rubella virus entry in airway and placental cells.
journal_articles.abstract: Rubella virus (RuV) causes rubella and, when acquired during pregnancy, congenital rubella syndrome1. Despite its clinical significance, the cellular entry mechanism of RuV remains poorly characterized, owing to limited identification of host receptors2, which hinders pathogenesis research and therapeutic development. Here, using proximity biotin labelling-based proteomics coupled with CRISPR-Cas9 validation, we identify nectin-4 as a functional RuV entry receptor. Ectopic expression of nectin-4 conferred susceptibility to RuV in non-permissive cells, whereas blocking or genetic ablation of nectin-4 reduced infection, results that demonstrate that nectin-4 is a major entry factor. Mechanistically, nectin-4 directly interacts with the RuV envelope glycoprotein heterodimer and facilitates receptor-mediated endocytosis following initial calcium-dependent viral attachment to cellular lipids. In polarized airway epithelial models, nectin-4 mediates basolateral entry of RuV and supports apical progeny release, a finding that provides a molecular mechanism for respiratory transmission. In placental models, nectin-4 is highly expressed on syncytiotrophoblasts and facilitates infection at the maternal-fetal interface, although additional nectin-4-independent pathways contribute to infection of other trophoblast populations. Together, these data establish nectin-4 as a key factor for respiratory transmission and early placental infection of RuV and highlight it as a promising therapeutic target for the prevention of rubella and related diseases.

journal_articles.title: Observation of prethermal dynamical phase transitions and resonant melting.
journal_articles.abstract: The dynamics of isolated quantum systems following a sudden quench has a central role in many areas of material science, high-energy physics and quantum chemistry1-4. Such far-from-equilibrium quantum dynamics-which features complex phenomena with implications for thermalization, non-equilibrium phase transitions and Floquet phase engineering5-8-is challenging to study numerically, in particular, in high-dimensional systems9,10. Here we use a programmable neutral-atom quantum simulator11 to systematically explore quench dynamics in spin models with up to 180 qubits. By initializing the system in a product state and performing quenches across a broad parameter space, we discover several stable, qualitatively distinct dynamical regimes. We trace their robustness to Floquet-like prethermal steady states8 that are stabilized over exponentially long emergent timescales by strong dynamical constraints. We further observe sharp peaks in the dynamical response that are quantitatively explained by the structured melting of prethermalization through resonances. In two dimensions, we uncover a prethermally driven, first-order dynamical phase transition linked to the proliferation of Néel-order defects6,12, and probe it quantitatively using a generalized Clausius-Clapeyron test. Together, these results establish a programmable route to high-energy prethermal phase structure: long-lived dynamical phases, their resonant breakdown and a first-order dynamical phase transition that is not inherited from the equilibrium phase boundaries.

journal_articles.title: Opportunistically Detecting Signs of Hypertension on a Consumer Smartwatch.
journal_articles.abstract: Hypertension is a silent killer, with over half of affected adults unaware of their condition1,2. This lack of awareness is a major concern, as early intervention is critical for preventing major adverse cardiovascular events3,4. Here we show that applying artificial intelligence (AI) to multimodal waveforms (photoplethysmography and accelerometry) recorded using a widely available consumer smartwatch (AI-PPG-ACC-HTN), without any cuff calibration, can detect hypertension with accuracy levels comparable to traditional cuffed blood pressure (BP) devices in the existing clinical framework. We validated AI-PPG-ACC-HTN in a prospective, multicenter study of 196 diverse participants free from known cardiovascular disease and antihypertensive medication against gold-standard 24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring. Over seven days of real-world monitoring, AI-PPG-ACC-HTN detected hypertension with a sensitivity of 65.8% (95% CI, 54.0%-76.3%), specificity of 90.0% (95% CI, 83.2%-94.7%), and positive predictive value (PPV) of 80.6% (95% CI, 68.6%-89.6%). In comparison, initial office BP screening achieved a sensitivity of 55.3% (95% CI, 43.4%-66.7%), specificity of 90.0% (95% CI, 83.2%-94.7%) and PPV of 77.8% (95% CI, 64.4%-88.0%). These results highlight an opportunity for consumer smartwatches to facilitate population-level opportunistic hypertension screening by prompting at-risk individuals toward clinical assessment and confirmatory diagnosis using established cuff-based methodologies, offering an accessible tool to address this major public health challenge.

journal_articles.title: Synergy in viral-bacterial co-infection expedites algal bloom demise.
journal_articles.abstract: Algal bloom demise, often caused by viruses, is a major driver of carbon cycling in the surface ocean1,2. However, although blooms collapse synchronously, fewer than 30% of algal cells are actively infected by viruses3, indicating the involvement of additional mortality agents. Here we quantified tripartite interactions within a synthetic community composed of the abundant coccolithophore Gephyrocapsa huxleyi, bacteria and viruses isolated during a bloom. We found that bacteria significantly enhanced virus-induced algal mortality in G. huxleyi as well as in three other globally widespread microalgae. We quantified this interaction using two new metrics: the synergy index, which measures viral-bacterial interaction strength, and the benefit index, which assesses changes in bacterial fitness. We identified Alteromonas bacteria as drivers of viral-bacterial co-infection, with consistently high synergy index and benefit index. We found that during algal blooms, Alteromonas displayed high chemoattraction towards infected cell extracts, accumulated in aggregates derived from bloom demise, and increased in abundance during oceanic bloom collapse. Viral-bacterial synergy represents a previously unrecognized mortality agent that controls bloom termination, modulating the balance between the carbon-recycling viral shunt and the carbon-exporting viral shuttle pathways, which influence global carbon cycling4-6.

journal_articles.title: The deep Earth origin of the Great Unconformity.
journal_articles.abstract: The Great Unconformity marks a globally extensive erosive surface linked to climatic shifts1 and environmental transitions2 that preceded the Cambrian explosion of life. The processes proposed to explain the formation of the Great Unconformity include glacial erosion during the Snowball Earth1,3,4, rifting and plume activity5-7, sea-level fall8 and mantle-driven dynamic topography6,9-11. However, the dynamics of these processes have not been tested. Here we show that continental-scale uplift and subsidence associated with long-wavelength dynamic topography12 due to mantle convection drove the formation and preservation of the Great Unconformity. Our models predict prolonged continental-scale Neoproterozoic uplift and long-term Phanerozoic subsidence for Laurentia, Baltica and North China. This vertical motion scenario is ideal for the formation and preservation of the Great Unconformity, which is a first-order surface expression of deep Earth processes. The predicted prolonged continental uplift throughout Cryogenian times would have resulted in marked erosion due to the action of glaciers13. The large area of Laurentia and limited deformation at its margins explain why the Great Unconformity is best preserved and documented there. Our models predict cycles of dynamic topography that are broadly reflected in preserved sediment volume across continents1,14, and open new avenues for understanding the environments of Cambrian animal diversification.

journal_articles.title: The neural basis of flavour-nutrient learning.
journal_articles.abstract: Animals learn about the external world in part through interoceptive signals1,2. For example, the nutrient content of food is first estimated in the mouth, in the form of flavour, and then it is measured again through slower signals from the gut. How these signals from the mouth and gut are integrated to drive learning is unclear. Here we identify a dopamine (DA) pathway that enables learning about the nutrient content of food. We show that DA neurons in the ventral tegmental area are necessary for associating nutrients with flavours, and that post-ingestive nutrients trigger DA release selectively in a small region of the anterior basolateral amygdala (BLA) but not in canonical DA targets in striatum. This nutrient-triggered DA release occurs preferentially in the left BLA in mice, and this same structure is preferentially activated by post-ingestive nutrients in humans. We identify the gut sensors that are responsible for nutrient-triggered DA release; show that they activate BLA-projecting DA neurons defined by expression of cholecystokinin; and demonstrate that stimulation of DA axon terminals in the anterior BLA drives flavour-nutrient learning but not other aspects of feeding behaviour. Two-photon imaging of neurons in the left anterior BLA reveals that they integrate gustatory and post-ingestive cues, and silencing these neurons prevents flavour-nutrient learning. These findings establish a neural basis for how animals learn about the nutrient content of their food.

journal_articles.title: Towards observing interstitial hydrogen in solution in metal lattices.
journal_articles.abstract: Hydrogen-bearing materials are central to low-carbon energy technologies1, but hydrogen itself is difficult to detect and localize at the nanoscale2-6. This hinders the development of advanced materials with better efficiency. Atom probe tomography (APT) can map hydrogen in three dimensions and at high resolution, yet characterization of dilute, mobile, interstitial hydrogen in metals has remained challenging because of low solubility, the ambiguity owing to hydrogen trapping by structural defects, as well as the artefacts introduced during hydrogen introduction4-6. Here we address whether interstitial hydrogen in solution in materials can be distinguished from defect-trapped hydrogen in APT. Using deuterium as a proxy for hydrogen, together with face-centred cubic (FCC) multi-principal-element alloys (MPEAs) containing coherent FCC precipitates, we show that deuterium atoms reproducibly concentrate in hydrogen-affinitive phases in a manner consistent with theoretical predictions. We further resolve differences in deuterium content between phases with distinct local chemistries and crystal structures, consistent with their different calculated hydrogen solution energies. These findings demonstrate that APT can move beyond identifying hydrides and solute-decorated defects to examine hydrogen in solid solution, providing new insights into hydrogen partitioning in structural alloys and informing materials design for hydrogen-related applications.

journal_articles.title: Tracing the spread of Celtic languages using ancient genomics.
journal_articles.abstract: Celtic languages are today restricted to Europe's Atlantic fringes but were widely spoken across the continent during the Iron Age1-3. How Celtic achieved this early distribution remains contested4, with alternative archaeological and linguistic models proposing different homelands and dispersal routes. Here we analyse genome-wide data from 4,587 ancient individuals, focusing on Bronze and Iron Age Europe, to test the extent to which these models fit reconstructed demographic histories. We identify three main processes shaping European population structure that are relevant to the Celtic dispersal. First, the arrival of Steppe-related ancestry with Bell Beaker-associated groups after around 4400 BP (calibrated years before present or 1950 CE) across the region in which Celtic and related languages were later spoken. Second, a movement from southwestern Europe into Britain during the Bronze Age (3800-3200 BP), consistent with scenarios in which Celtic formed along the Atlantic façade. Third, a westward expansion of ancestry related to Late Bronze Age Knovíz-Urnfield-associated populations from eastern central Europe (3200-2800 BP), affecting France, the British Isles, northeastern Iberia and Italy and later associated with Iron Age Hallstatt and La Tène contexts5-8. Although all three movements have parallels with proposed models, we argue that the final movement, from eastern central Europe, is most parsimonious for the spread of Celtic. Although human history does not necessarily follow a parsimonious trajectory9 and language shifts need not track genetic change, these results delimit the demographic scenarios that are plausible for the emergence of Celtic in prehistoric Europe.

journal_articles.title: Tracing the spread of Germanic languages using ancient genomics.
journal_articles.abstract: Germanic languages, including German, English, Frisian, Dutch and the Nordic languages, are widely spoken across northwest Europe. However, the timing and location of the prehistoric arrival of this Indo-European linguistic phylum, as well as its Iron Age diversification, remain contentious1-3. Here, by sequencing 712 ancient human genomes and analysing them alongside 4,009 previously published genomes, we identify an archaeologically elusive population that entered Sweden, likely from the Baltic region, by around 4000 BP. This population, which became widespread throughout Scandinavia by 3500 BP, offers a potential vector for the introduction of the Germanic language group to Scandinavia4-6, some 800 years later than traditionally assumed7-9. Following the Late Iron Age disintegration of Germanic into its descendant languages, we observe by 1650 BP a southward migration from southern Scandinavia into presumed Celtic-speaking areas, including present-day Germany, Poland and the Netherlands. During the subsequent Migration Period (1575-1375 BP), we see this ancestry among Germanic-speaking Anglo-Saxons in Britain and Langobards in southern Europe. In the same time period, we identify a related large-scale northward back-migration into Denmark and southern Sweden, coinciding with the rise of Danish influence and the linguistically documented emergence of Old Norse. These findings indicate that multiple migrations and geographical locations had a major role in the arrival and formation of Germanic, as well as in its divergence into historical and modern descendant languages.

journal_articles.title: Twist-angle-dependent quantum phase diagrams in moiré bilayer MoTe2.
journal_articles.abstract: Two-dimensional semiconducting moiré superlattices provide a highly tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated and topological quantum phases1-5. As a prototypical example, twisted bilayer MoTe2 (tMoTe2) has been shown to host fractional topological phases at zero magnetic field6-20. However, their evolution with twist angle and competition with other correlated quantum states remain largely unexplored. Here we report a systematic transport study of twist-angle-dependent phase diagrams in tMoTe2 across a range of 3.79°-5.76°, revealing an evolution from valley-polarized, fractional topological states to valley-degenerate correlated states and superconductivity. At relatively small twist angles, partially filled Chern bands of tMoTe2 host fractional quantum anomalous Hall states following the Jain sequence, together with signatures of an anomalous composite Fermi liquid at moiré hole filling factor νh = 1/2. Increasing twist angle progressively suppresses fractional topological phases and reconstructs the half-filled Chern band into symmetry-breaking integer Chern insulating states. At νh = 1, we observe a transition from robust integer quantum anomalous Hall insulators at small angles to displacement-field-tuned, topologically trivial correlated insulators at larger angles. At twist angles above approximately 5.6°, superconductivity emerges adjacent to the νh = 1 correlated insulator, with a phase diagram closely resembling that recently reported in twisted bilayer WSe2 (refs. 21-24). Our results indicate a unified twist-angle-driven phase evolution linking fractional topology, symmetry breaking, magnetic order and superconductivity, providing new insight into the emergent quantum phenomena in moiré systems.

journal_articles.title: Methylated eEF1A selectively decodes mRNA to shape cancer proteomes.
journal_articles.abstract: Although mRNA decoding efficiency influences protein synthesis, it remains unknown whether the translation elongation machinery harbours intrinsic mechanisms that selectively modulate codon decoding to shape proteomes. Here we show that METTL13-catalysed dimethylation of the elongation factor eEF1A at lysine 55 (eEF1AK55me2) enhances decoding of select codons, preferentially increasing pro-oncogenic protein synthesis to promote tumorigenesis and targeted therapy resistance. Proteomic profiling and single-molecule imaging reveal that eEF1AK55me2 increases decoding efficiency, particularly for under-represented codons with weak wobble-position base pairing. In cancer cells, METTL13 knockdown reduced translation of oncogenic mRNA enriched in eEF1AK55me2-dependent codons, including KRAS; synonymous recoding with eEF1AK55me2-independent codons reversed this effect. METTL13 loss inhibited the growth of KRASG12C inhibitor (sotorasib)-resistant lung adenocarcinoma syngeneic tumours and patient-derived xenografts. In relapsed autochthonous KRASG12C-driven lung adenocarcinoma, METTL13 ablation mitigated sotorasib resistance and significantly extended survival in vivo. Among patients receiving a KRASG12C inhibitor, inferred METTL13 activity was associated with inferior clinical response. These findings identify an eEF1AK55me2-mediated mRNA decoding mechanism promoting selective oncogenic protein synthesis and suggest METTL13 targeting may counteract KRAS-inhibitor resistance.

journal_articles.title: STING-dependent TNF signalling promotes IKKβ-mediated ATG9A phosphorylation and autophagy.
journal_articles.abstract: Chemotherapeutic drugs, either alone or in combination with immunotherapy, are routinely used in cancer treatment. However, cancer cells frequently develop resistance to chemotherapy, and the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Using head and neck squamous cell carcinoma as a model, we show that chemotherapy activates the cGAS-STING pathway, leading to the induction of TNF. TNF mediates a paracrine signalling pathway in recipient tumour cells, leading to IKKβ activation and ATG9A phosphorylation at serine 654, thereby promoting autophagy. Moreover, IKKβ activation and ATG9A S654 phosphorylation are induced by TNF, nutrient deprivation and mTOR inhibition, suggesting that the IKKβ-ATG9A axis may represent a common regulatory mechanism of autophagy. Analysis of patient samples further reveals that chemotherapy induces autophagy, and elevated phosphorylation of ATG9A at S654 correlates with poor chemotherapy response. Of note, TNF blockade enhances therapeutic efficacy in both chemotherapy alone and chemotherapy combined with immune checkpoint inhibition. Together, our findings uncover a previously unrecognized TNF-IKKβ-ATG9A signalling axis that promotes autophagy and highlight TNF blockade as a promising strategy to overcome chemotherapy resistance.

journal_articles.title: A CCL21 gene-modified dendritic cell vaccine combined with pembrolizumab in advanced non-small cell lung cancer: a phase I trial.
journal_articles.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed treatment for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but resistance to these therapies is common. We report here results from a phase I trial combining intratumoral injection of a CCL21-expressing dendritic cell (CCL21-DC) vaccine with pembrolizumab in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03546361). The primary objectives were to determine the maximum administered dose (MAD) in the dose escalation phase and the objective response rate (ORR) in the dose expansion. Eleven patients were enrolled in the dose escalation cohort, and 12 patients were treated in the dose expansion cohort at the MAD of 3 ×107 cells/injection. The trial did not meet its primary endpoint for ORR as no objective responses were observed, though 36.8% of patients achieved a best response of stable disease. The combination therapy was well tolerated. Post-hoc analyses of longitudinal biopsies revealed that the therapy increased tumor infiltration by CD4+ T cells and novel T cell clones. Disease stability was associated with increased T cell receptor diversity and greater expansion of novel clones following therapy. However, many novel clones failed to persist over time, and immunosuppressive myeloid signaling signatures were identified across time points. Our findings overall demonstrated that CCL21-DC vaccination combined with pembrolizumab can promote T cell infiltration, but this did not translate into meaningful clinical efficacy, potentially due to limited tumor specificity of the T cell response and an inability to fully reprogram the tumor microenvironment.

journal_articles.title: A Robust Gel Polymer Electrode with Controlled-Release Polymerization towards Practical Lithium-Sulfur Batteries.
journal_articles.abstract: While rational electrode engineering has promoted the kinetics of lithium-sulfur batteries, persistent lithium polysulfide diffusion continues to undermine the cyclability of conventional liquid electrolyte systems. We propose a quasi-solid gel electrode design that integrates the sulfur species-blocking attributes of a solid-state system within a liquid electrolyte framework. This is achieved through a well-designed free radical-controlled-release polymerization strategy, which precisely governs the formation of a processable poly(ethyl cyanoacrylate) network. This approach enables secondary in situ gelation triggered by electrolyte infiltration, forming gel-phase electrode architectures. Mechanistically, the resulting gel-based electrode provides dynamically adaptive stress dissipation to accommodate volume variations, establishes continuous ion-permeable pathways for deeper positive electrode discharge, and acts as a synergistic physico-chemical barrier for sulfur species confinement. As a result, the positive electrode delivers a high initial capacity of 812.8 mA h g-1 at 2 C and sustains stable cycling operation over 1000 cycles. A 1.7 Ah-level pouch cell demonstrates potential for a sustained power supply for an unmanned aerial vehicle.

journal_articles.title: A convergent total synthesis of the ivermectin aglycon through transition metal-mediated and anionic transformations.
journal_articles.abstract: For decades, the avermectin class of macrolide natural products have played a critical role in the treatment of numerous infectious diseases and pests across the globe. Due to their biological activity and complex architecture, these natural products have inspired a great number of influential syntheses. Herein, we report a convergent total synthesis of the ivermectin B1a aglycon that addresses long‑standing challenges in constructing its highly functionalized macrolide framework. Systematic evaluation of multiple cyclization pathways for the southern hydrobenzofuran fragment leads to the development of a palladium‑catalyzed reductive cyclization of an alkynyl ketone, which reliably forges the benzofuran core while constructing a congested tetra-substituted stereocenter. The northern spiroacetal fragment is efficiently assembled through an epoxide ring-opening cascade using simple building blocks. A cyclization templating strategy employing a flexible succinate linker is leveraged to overcome the kinetic and thermodynamic challenges associated with macrocyclization. Ultimately, this strategy enables the selective ring-closing metathesis to forge the 21‑membered macrocycle, providing access to ivermectin B1a aglycon in 21 longest‑linear steps from p-cresol.

journal_articles.title: A cytidine deaminase biodegrader sensitises multiple cancer types to deoxycytidine analogue-based chemotherapies.
journal_articles.abstract: Deoxycytidine (dC) analogues are widely used to treat solid tumours and blood cancers. However, their clinical efficacy is often limited by resistance mediated by cytidine deaminase (CDA), which converts these drugs into inactive metabolites. Existing CDA inhibitors have limited efficacy and off-target effects, highlighting the need for alternative approaches. Here, we show the development of a CDA biodegrader, an intracellular anti-CDA VHH fused to the SPOP E3 ubiquitin ligase, enabling specific CDA degradation. It effectively depletes CDA in pancreatic, lung, and acute myeloid leukaemia cancer cell lines, increasing sensitivity to dC analogues in vitro. Combined with gemcitabine, the CDA biodegrader inhibits pancreatic and lung tumour growth in vivo. Importantly, mRNA encoding the biodegrader delivered using virus-like particles achieves efficient sensitisation to gemcitabine in vitro and in vivo. This proof-of-concept study establishes targeted CDA degradation as a feasible strategy to enhance the therapeutic efficacy of dC analogues.

journal_articles.title: A generative diffusion framework for physically consistent 3D turbulence.
journal_articles.abstract: Synthesizing fully developed three-dimensional turbulence remains a long-standing problem in fluid mechanics and an open challenge for generative modeling. This difficulty arises from extreme dimensionality, multiscale fluctuations, strong intermittency, and the need to satisfy exact physical constraints, including incompressibility and prescribed mass and momentum fluxes under given boundary conditions. We propose a physics-constrained diffusion model in which some a priori constraints can be incorporated directly into the generative dynamics. Using rotating turbulence as a paradigmatic system with key geophysical applications, we assess the proposed framework. Here, we show that it enables stable and statistically faithful single-time synthesis of inertial-range three-dimensional turbulent velocity fields, accurately reproducing anisotropic energy spectra, intermittent statistics, and physical constraints, whereas standard denoising diffusion probabilistic models exhibit multiscale statistical deviations, violations of physical consistency, and substantially slower training convergence, thereby pointing to broader implications for generative modeling of high-dimensional, physically constrained complex systems.

journal_articles.title: A multimeric pore complex in the poxvirus core revealed by integrative structural analysis.
journal_articles.abstract: It has long been known that poxviruses transcribe more than a hundred early mRNAs within their viral core, yet how these transcripts exit the core remains unknown. Here, we combine cryo-electron tomography with deep-learning-based particle picking, subtomogram averaging, cross-linking mass spectrometry, and AlphaFold3 modeling to resolve the molecular architecture of a long-sought pore within the poxvirus core. The pore is formed by a heteromeric assembly of the viral proteins E8, E6, and L3, which together create a hollow hexameric tube spanning both the core wall and the surface-exposed palisade layer. Within the pore channel, we observe a rod-like density consistent with the viral RNA helicase I8, which may contribute to the release of the newly synthesized viral mRNAs from the core. We further observe a state of the pore lacking the outer and basal rings under transcription conditions. Together, our findings identify the structure and dynamics of a candidate mRNA-release pore within the surface layer of a double-stranded DNA virus and suggest that it may form part of the poxvirus transcription machinery.

journal_articles.title: A multiplexed wearable microfluidic platform for non-invasive sweat-inspired monitoring of plant guttation biomarkers.
journal_articles.abstract: Plant guttation fluid provides a chemically informative readout of internal plant status, offering an externally accessible window into plant physiological processes. However, its minute volume, intermittent availability, and susceptibility to evaporation limit its use for continuous biochemical monitoring. Here we introduce PlantIonics, an integrated on-leaf microfluidic electrochemical platform for real-time, non-invasive monitoring of guttation biomarkers and leaf microenvironment. A bioinspired wedge-shaped microchannel with asymmetric wettability achieves rapid (0.6 s) and unidirectional self-driven fluid collection, providing a continuously refreshed sensing interface for dynamic guttation profiling. Combined with a multichannel sensor array and a compact wireless flexible printed circuit board, PlantIonics simultaneously measures guttation-fluid biomarkers (potassium, sodium, glucose) and local leaf microenvironment. Multi-day on-plant studies demonstrate stress-responsive guttation fluctuations that correlate with root-level ionic perturbations and light modulation, demonstrating the platform's capability to monitor dynamic physiological regulation. PlantIonics establishes a sweat-inspired analytical framework for non-invasive plant monitoring, offering opportunities for early stress diagnostics, field phenotyping, and precision agriculture.
